newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets dragged lower by Wall Street woes.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets dragged lower by Wall Street woes.

text.p: Markets across Asia retreated on Thursday after Wall Street's overnight plunge, with Hong Kong falling 136 points, or one percent.
On Wednesday, the Dow skidded 71 points, or 1.09 percent, to about 6,403 after falling nearly 130 points earlier.
The result was a slide for nearly every Asian bourse.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index shed 1.03 percent or 136.32 points to close at 13,053.28.
"This (fall) is a reaction to the S&P and the Dow," said Philip Pang, managing director of Amsteel Securities.
Institutional profit-taking dominated afternoon activity in Hong Kong, brokers said.
A technical glitch caused chaos at the open, when the index was erroneously shown to have dropped more than 500 points.
Tokyo stocks finished on a feeble note but well off their lows. The hefty fall on Wall Street weighed on sentiment, brokers said.
The Nikkei 225 closed down 67.18 points or 0.33 percent at 20,501.20.
"Domestic fundamentals have not changed much and the market wants to see whether Wall Street recovers from the sharp fall on Wednesday," a "Big Four" broker said.
Philippine shares were sharply lower at the close of trading. The composite index shed 31.65 points, or 1.0 pct, to 3129.11.
"It's the Dow Jones again," said Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Equities.

Australian shares ended with a loss of 19.7 points or 0.83 percent at 2339.6. Local investors ignored positive employment data and followed their nervous U.S. counterparts out of equities, brokers said.
New Zealand's NZSE-40 Capital Index finished 15.01 points lower to 2,362.52. The Singapore benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index eased 9.9 points to 2,182.55 at the close of trading.

Malaysian stocks were also hit by Wall Street's fall and lingering jitters following Wednesday's bout of negative rumours, traders said. Kuala Lumpur's Composite Index sagged to end 4.7 points weaker to 1,199.69.

Thai stocks took a beating with the SET index down 13.61 points or 1.54 percent to 872.25 at the close. Brokers said investors offloaded shares across the board, in line with poor sentiment in other regional markets.
In South Korea, stocks closed at a new three-year low, dragged down by heavy institutional selling near the end of trading, brokers said.
The composite index finished down 15.30 points or a hefty 2.17 percent to 689.38, its lowest close since September 18, 1993.
Indonesian shares defied the regional trend to close higher, helped by gains in market heavyweight, Telkom. The Jakarta Composite Index ended up 1.33 points or 0.21 percent at 627.90.
Taiwan stocks also escaped the regional downturn, finishing at 6,825.62, a gain of 22.88 points or 0.34 percent.
Brokers said big-capital shares and blue chips attracted most buying.
The dollar was mixed in late Tokyo. At 1208 GMT, the dollar traded at 113.19/29 yen and 1.5456/66 marks.
After slow trading, Hong Kong gold bullion ended a tad higher at US$368.70/369.20 an ounce against New York's US$368.60/369.10 close on Wednesday.
SIMEX Brent crude futures ended firmer in a quiet market, following the overnight plunge on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
January Brent was last traded at $22.45 a barrel, 30 cents over the last IPE close.
